results.summary: This design generates a VGA video signal that animates columns of pink hearts transitioning on and off the screen. It is implemented in Verilog using the VGA Playground environment and is intended to be tested by running the simulation and observing the output. The design requires a VGA monitor connected to the Tiny VGA PMOD pinout. The project is a playful visual demonstration rather than a practical application.

This analog tile integrates two independent circuits: a current-controlled ring oscillator VCO and a differential amplifier, sharing a single bias/control pin. It is implemented at the transistor level and requires external test equipment such as a DC supply, function generator, and oscilloscope or frequency counter. The design is intended for analog experimentation and characterization. No digital interface is used.

This project implements a 16-bit configurable Galois LFSR (Linear Feedback Shift Register) designed for Tiny Tapeout SKY130. It is implemented in Verilog and can be configured to use different feedback taps. The design is intended for digital logic experimentation and can be tested with standard digital inputs and outputs. It is a classic pseudo-random number generator circuit.

This project implements a multiplier and ALU design in Verilog. It is intended for digital arithmetic operations and can be tested with standard digital inputs and outputs. The design is a combinational or sequential logic block that performs multiplication and arithmetic logic functions. It is a basic building block for more complex digital systems.

This project implements a programmable I/O (PIO) block inspired by the RP2350's PIO but not compatible with it. It is written in SystemVerilog and includes a finite state machine for controlling the I/O. The design is intended for flexible digital I/O operations and can be tested with standard digital inputs and outputs. It is a reconfigurable logic block for custom I/O protocols.

This project generates music-like tones using a PWM output that can drive a buzzer. It is implemented in Verilog and uses a pseudo-random number generator and LFSR for stochastic sound generation. The design requires a PMOD buzzer for audio output. It is a simple sound generator for experimentation.
